text: Separate the vote from the work
After this you can record a change decision and follow it to completion.

A designated change authority may accept, decline or postpone a proposal. A review board is one decision method. Its authority comes from project rules, not from holding a meeting. Record the result, conditions and rationale. After accepting a change, release controlled work. Update affected descriptions and record completion evidence for each relevant unit. A signed decision is not evidence that a workshop has finished.

items: Confirm the proposed decision is within the group's authority. You should see: The correct approver is identified. If not: Refer an out-of-scope decision to the assigned higher role.
Record the outcome and its conditions. You should see: The decision can be understood later. If not: Correct incomplete minutes before acting.
Issue the approved work and document updates. You should see: Implementers have the right instructions. If not: Do not infer scope from informal comments.
Track work and verify completion by unit or release. You should see: Status is based on evidence. If not: Keep incomplete items open even if approval is final.
A board accepts an enclosure change for the next production batch. Existing example units stay on their earlier approved version unless the decision explicitly includes retrofit work.

text: An approval is a controlled instruction, not proof of completed installation.
Some organizations do not use a formal board; the named authority still matters.

items: Closing the change record after the meeting Different units may be at different implementation stages. Fix: Track completion separately and retain evidence.
